entries.label: available carbohydrate
entries.definition: Carbohydrates that are absorbed in the small intestine and provide carbohydrate for metabolism in monogastric animals.

entries.label: free sugar
entries.definition: Available carbohydrate in monosaccharide and disaccharide form

entries.label: soluble dietary fibre
entries.definition: Dietary fibre which dissolves in water and is partially or completely fermented in the colon of monogastric animals by gut bacteria.

entries.label: resistant starch
entries.definition: A portion of starch that cannot be digested by amylases in the small intestine

entries.label: gum
entries.definition: A complex carbohydrate with various rheological properties that result in viscoelastic behavior

entries.label: viscous dietary fibre
entries.definition: Soluble dietary fibre that dissolves in water to form semifluid solutions or a gel-like matrix, and exhibits high shear strength in aqueous solutions.

entries.label: soluble dietary fibre precipitate (SDFP)
entries.definition: Water soluble dietary fibre which precipitates in 78% aqueous ethanol.

entries.label: soluble dietary fibre soluble (SDFS)
entries.definition: Water soluble dietary fibre which remains soluble in 78% aqueous ethanol.

entries.label: low molecular weight dietary fibre
entries.definition: Dietary fibre oligomers of degree of polymerization (DP) > 2 which remain soluble in 78% aqueous ethanol and are not digested by enzymes of the human digestive tract.

entries.label: non-starch polysaccharide
entries.definition: A polysaccharide fraction of dietary fibre that excludes lignin and all starch.

entries.label: cellulosic polysaccharide
entries.definition: A non-starch polysaccharide composed of cellulose or its derivatives.

entries.label: non-starch non-cellulosic polysaccharide
entries.definition: A non-starch polysaccharide, other than cellulose, composed of chains of various types of monosaccharide units, that may be substituted with side chains and by various functional groups.

entries.label: pullulan
entries.definition: A linear α-glucan composed of repeating α-1,4-linked maltotriose or maltotetraose subunits, connected by α-1,6-glycosidic bonds.

entries.label: modified cellulose
entries.definition: A cellulosic polysaccharide to which substituent groups have been added.

entries.label: chitin-glucan
entries.definition: A non-starch polysaccharide composed of chitin (β-1,4-poly-N-acetyl-D-glucosamine) and β-1,3-D-glucan, obtained from Aspergillus niger mycelial cell walls.

entries.label: nondigestible oligosaccharide
entries.definition: A dietary fiber consisting of 3-9 monomeric units not digested by enzymes of the human digestive tract and soluble in water.

entries.label: graminan
entries.definition: A fructan consisting primarily of β-(2,6)-linked fructose residues with β-(1,2)-branches

entries.label: pectic polysaccharide
entries.definition: A polysaccharide primarily composed of a backbone containing α−1,4-D-galacturonic acid residues

entries.label: polysaccharide-based hydrocolloid
entries.definition: A highly water-soluble or water-dispersible polysaccharide that readily dissolves or disperses to form highly hydrated entities of colloidal (nanoscale) dimensions

entries.label: arabinoxylan-oligosaccharide
entries.definition: A nondigestible oligosaccharide composed of a backbone of β-(1→4)-linked d-xylopyranosyl residues partially substituted with arabinofuranosyl side chains.

entries.label: gingerol
entries.definition: A beta-hydroxy ketone that is 5-hydroxydecan-3-one substituted by a 4-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl moiety at position 1; believed to inhibit adipogenesis. It is a constituent of fresh ginger.

entries.label: sodium ascorbate
entries.definition: An organic sodium salt resulting from the replacement of the proton from the 3-hydroxy group of ascorbic acid by a sodium ion.

entries.label: sodium benzoate
entries.definition: An organic sodium salt resulting from the replacement of the proton from the carboxy group of benzoic acid by a sodium ion.

entries.label: sodium disulfite
entries.definition: An inorganic sodium salt composed of sodium and disulfite ions in a 2:1 ratio.

entries.label: vitamin A
entries.definition: Any member of a group of fat-soluble retinoids produced via metabolism of provitamin A carotenoids that exhibit biological activity against vitamin A deficiency. Vitamin A is involved in immune function, vision, reproduction, and cellular communication.

entries.label: potassium carbonate
entries.definition: A potassium salt that is the dipotassium salt of carbonic acid.

entries.label: 7,10,13,16-docosatetraenoic acid
entries.definition: A docosatetraenoic acid in which the four double bonds are located at positions 7, 10, 13 and 16 (geometry unspecified).

entries.label: sodium propionate
entries.definition: An organic sodium salt comprising equal numbers of sodium and propionate ions.

entries.label: fatty acid 18:3
entries.definition: Any trienoic fatty acid containing 18 carbons.

entries.label: bentonite
entries.definition: An aluminosilicate mineral consisting mostly of montmorillonite. The different types of bentonite (aluminium bentonite; calcium bentonite; potassium bentonite; sodium bentonite) are named after their dominant element.

entries.label: glycol
entries.definition: A diol in which the two hydroxy groups are on different carbon atoms, usually but not necessarily adjacent.

entries.label: 4-hydroxy-all-trans-beta-carotene
entries.definition: A beta-carotene carrying one additional hydroxy substituent at position 4.

entries.label: cellulose acetate
entries.definition: A glucan derivative obtained through the esterification of cellulose by acetic anhydride or acetic acid, resulting in the substitution of some of the hydroxy groups of cellulose by acetyl groups. It is used in a variety of applications including base material for photographic film, clothing, membrane filters, coatings, food packaging, and as a frame material for eyeglasses.

entries.label: isomalt
entries.definition: A diastereoisomeric mixture composed of 1-O-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-D-mannitol dihydrate and 6-O-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-D-glucitol in a 1:1 ratio. It is used in the food industry as a sugar substitute and in the pharmaceutical industry as a tabletting excipient.

entries.label: retinyl palmitate
entries.definition: A palmitate ester of retinol with undefined geometry about the C=C bonds.

entries.label: choline
entries.definition: A choline that is the parent compound of the cholines class, consisting of ethanolamine having three methyl substituents attached to the amino function.

entries.label: cysteine
entries.definition: A sulfur-containing amino acid that is propanoic acid with an amino group at position 2 and a sulfanyl group at position 3.

entries.label: acetic acid
entries.definition: A simple monocarboxylic acid containing two carbons.

entries.label: glycine
entries.definition: The simplest (and the only achiral) proteinogenic amino acid, with a hydrogen atom as its side chain.

entries.label: 5-formyltetrahydrofolic acid
entries.definition: A formyltetrahydrofolic acid in which the formyl group is located at position 5.

entries.label: 2,3-dihydroxybutanedioic acid
entries.definition: A tetraric acid that is butanedioic acid substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 2 and 3.

entries.label: aldose
entries.definition: Aldehydic parent sugars (polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H, n ≥ 2) and their intramolecular hemiacetals.

entries.label: L-alpha-amino acid
entries.definition: Any α-amino acid having <small>L</small>-configuration at the α-carbon.

entries.label: succinic acid
entries.definition: An α,ω-dicarboxylic acid resulting from the formal oxidation of each of the terminal methyl groups of butane to the corresponding carboxy group. It is an intermediate metabolite in the citric acid cycle.

entries.label: hexadecanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain, sixteen-carbon, saturated long-chain fatty acid.

entries.label: polypeptide
entries.definition: A peptide containing ten or more amino acid residues.

entries.label: arachidonic acid
entries.definition: A long-chain fatty acid that is a C20, polyunsaturated fatty acid having four (Z)-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11 and 14.

entries.label: long-chain fatty acid
entries.definition: A fatty acid with a chain length ranging from C<small><sub>13</sub></small> to C<small><sub>22</sub></small>.

entries.label: nicotinic acid
entries.definition: A pyridinemonocarboxylic acid that is pyridine in which the hydrogen at position 3 is replaced by a carboxy group.

entries.label: lycopene
entries.definition: An acyclic carotene commonly obtained from tomatoes and other red fruits.

entries.label: biotin
entries.definition: An organic heterobicyclic compound that consists of 2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazole having a valeric acid substituent attached to the tetrahydrothiophene ring. The parent of the class of biotins.

entries.label: D-mannose
entries.definition: A mannose with D-configuration.

entries.label: pyrogallol
entries.definition: A  benzenetriol carrying hydroxy groups at positions 1, 2 and 3.

entries.label: oleic acid
entries.definition: An octadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at C-9 has Z (cis) stereochemistry.

entries.label: urea
entries.definition: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups. The commercially available fertilizer has an analysis of 46-0-0 (N-P2O5-K2O).

entries.label: chitosan
entries.definition: An aminoglycan consisting of beta-(1->4)-linked D-glucosamine residues.

entries.label: menaquinone
entries.definition: Any member of the class of menaquinones that is 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone with an unsaturated isoprenoid chain at the 3-position.

entries.label: alanine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that consists of propionic acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2.

entries.label: carbon dioxide
entries.definition: A one-carbon compound with formula CO<small><sub>2</sub></small> in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

entries.label: raffinose
entries.definition: A trisaccharide composed of alpha-D-galactopyranose, alpha-D-glucopyranose and beta-D-fructofuranose joined in sequence by 1->6 and 1<->2 glycosidic linkages, respectively.

entries.label: carbohydrate
entries.definition: Any member of the class of organooxygen compounds that is a polyhydroxy-aldehyde or -ketone or a lactol resulting from their intramolecular condensation (monosaccharides); substances derived from these by reduction of the carbonyl group (alditols), by oxidation of one or more hydroxy groups to afford the corresponding aldehydes, ketones, or carboxylic acids, or by replacement of one or more hydrox

entries.label: peptide
entries.definition: Amide derived from two or more amino carboxylic acid molecules (the same or different) by formation of a covalent bond from the carbonyl carbon of one to the nitrogen atom of another with formal loss of water. The term is usually applied to structures formed from α-amino acids, but it includes those derived from any amino carboxylic acid. X = OH, OR, NH2, NHR, etc.

entries.label: cis-fatty acid
entries.definition: A cis configuration means that the two hydrogen atoms adjacent to the double bond stick out on the same side of the chain. The rigidity of the double bond freezes its conformation and, in the case of the cis isomer, causes the chain to bend and restricts the conformational freedom of the fatty acid. The more double bonds the chain has in the cis configuration, the less flexibility it has. When a c

entries.label: trans-fatty acid
entries.definition: A trans configuration in contrast to the cis, means that the adjacent two hydrogen atoms lie on opposite sides of the chain. As a result, they do not cause the chain to bend much, and their shape is similar to straight saturated fatty acids.

entries.label: nucleoside 5'-phosphate
entries.definition: A ribosyl or deoxyribosyl derivative of a pyrimidine or purine base in which C-5 of the ribose ring is mono-, di-, tri- or tetra-phosphorylated.

entries.label: pyridoxine
entries.definition: A hydroxymethylpyridine with hydroxymethyl groups at positions 4 and 5, a hydroxy group at position 3 and a methyl group at position 2. The 4-methanol form of vitamin B6, it is converted intoto pyridoxal phosphate which is a coenzyme for synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters, sphingolipids and aminolevulinic acid.

entries.label: cyanidin 3-O-rutinoside chloride
entries.definition: A member of the class of anthocyanin chlorides that has cyanidin 3-O-rutinoside as the cationic counterpart.

entries.label: melatonin
entries.definition: A member of the class of acetamides that is acetamide in which one of the hydrogens attached to the nitrogen atom is replaced by a 2-(5-methoxy-1H-indol-3-yl)ethyl group. It is a hormone secreted by the pineal gland in humans.

entries.label: methionine
entries.definition: A sulfur-containing amino acid that is butyric acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2 and a methylthio substituent at position 4.

entries.label: heteroglycan
entries.definition: A polysaccharide composed of two or more different types of monosaccharides,

entries.label: propane-1,2-diol
entries.definition: The simplest member of the class of propane-1,2-diols, consisting of propane in which a hydrogen at position 1 and a hydrogen at position 2 are substituted by hydroxy groups. A colourless, viscous, hygroscopic, low-melting (−59°C) and high-boiling (188°C) liquid with low toxicity, it is used as a solvent, emulsifying agent, and antifreeze.

entries.label: riboflavin
entries.definition: D-Ribitol in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[g]pteridin-10(2H)-yl moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver, kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast. The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its principal forms in tissues and ce

entries.label: glucomannan
entries.definition: A heteroglycan consisting of beta-(1->4)-linked D-glucose (G) and D-mannose (M) in a proportion of 5:8. The basic polymeric repeating unit has the pattern: GGMMGMMMMMGGM, with branching through beta-(1->3)- and beta-(1->6)-glucosyl linkages. Acetate groups are present on C-6 every 9-19 units of the main chain.

entries.label: chitin
entries.definition: An aminoglycan consisting of beta-(1->4)-linked N-acetyl-D-glucosamine residues.

entries.label: dinitrogen oxide
entries.definition: A nitrogen oxide consisting of linear unsymmetrical molecules with formula N<small><sub>2</sub></small>O. While it is the most used gaseous anaesthetic in the world, its major commercial use, due to its solubility under pressure in vegetable fats combined with its non-toxicity in low concentrations, is as an aerosol spray propellant and aerating agent for canisters of 'whipped' cream.

entries.label: biphenyl
entries.definition: A benzenoid aromatic compound that consists of two benzene rings connected by a single covalent bond. Biphenyl occurs naturally in coal tar, crude oil, and natural gas. Formerly used as a fungicide for citrus crops.

entries.label: erythritol
entries.definition: The meso-diastereomer of butane-1,2,3,4-tetrol.

entries.label: xylitol
entries.definition: A pentitol (five-carbon sugar alcohol) having meso-configuration, being derived from xylose by reduction of the carbonyl group.

entries.label: nicotinamide
entries.definition: A pyridinecarboxamide that is pyridine in which the hydrogen at position 3 is replaced by a carboxamide group.

entries.label: stachyose
entries.definition: A tetrasaccharide consisting of sucrose having an alpha-D-galactosyl-(1->6)-alpha-D-galactosyl moiety attached at the 6-position of the glucose.

entries.label: IMP
entries.definition: A purine ribonucleoside 5'-monophosphate having hypoxanthine as the nucleobase.

entries.label: glucose
entries.definition: An aldohexose used as a source of energy and metabolic intermediate.

entries.label: maltose
entries.definition: A glycosylglucose consisting of two D-glucopyranose units connected by an alpha-(1->4)-linkage.

entries.label: pectin
entries.definition: Any mixture of complex, colloidal, macromolecular plant galacturonans containing a large proportion of D-galactopyranosyluronic acid residues in alpha-(1->4) linkage, the carboxy groups of which may be esterified to varying degrees by methyl groups or be partially or completely converted into salts. The structure shown is that of the parent polygalacturonan.

entries.label: all-trans-retinol
entries.definition: A retinol in which all four exocyclic double bonds have E- (trans-) geometry.

entries.label: linoleic acid
entries.definition: An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry.

entries.label: cystine
entries.definition: A sulfur-containing amino acid obtained by the oxidation of two cysteine molecules which are then linked via a disulfide bond.

entries.label: cyanocob(III)alamin
entries.definition: A complex cob(III)alamin in which cobalt is positioned in the centre of a planar corrin tetrapyrrole ring and bound axially to a 5,6-dimethylbenzimidazole moiety and a cyano group. It is one of several forms of the vitamin known as vitamin B12.

entries.label: alditol
entries.definition: A carbohydrate that is an acyclic polyol having the general formula HOCH2[CH(OH)]nCH2OH (formally derivable from an aldose by reduction of the carbonyl group).

entries.label: L-arabinopyranose
entries.definition: The six-membered ring form of L-arabinose.

entries.label: alginic acid
entries.definition: A linear copolymer macromolecule composed of homopolymeric blocks of 1→4-linked β-<small>D</small>-mannuronic acid and α-<small>L</small>-guluronic acid residues, covalently linked together in different sequences or blocks.

entries.label: L-cysteine

aliases.text: cysteine, l- and its hydrochlorides - sodium and potassium salts
aliases.norm: cysteine l and its hydrochlorides sodium and potassium salts

entries.definition: An optically active form of cysteine having <small>L</small>-configuration.

entries.label: beta-carotene
entries.definition: A cyclic carotene obtained by dimerisation of all-trans-retinol. A strongly-coloured red-orange pigment abundant in plants and fruit and the most active and important provitamin A carotenoid.

entries.label: maltooligosaccharide
entries.definition: A glucooligosaccharide derived from glucose monomers linked via α-<small>D</small>-1,4 bonds as in maltose.  The term is commonly applied to the series of linear oligosaccharides composed of two, three, four, five and six such units of glucose.

entries.label: D-aldohexose
entries.definition: Any <small>D</small>-aldose having a chain of six carbon atoms in the molecule.

entries.label: FMN
entries.definition: A flavin mononucleotide that is riboflavin (vitamin B<small><sub>2</sub></small>) in which the primary hydroxy group has been converted to its dihydrogen phosphate ester.

entries.label: cyclomaltodextrin
entries.definition: A cyclic oligosaccharide comprising a ring of <small>D</small>-glucose units linked by α-(1→4) glycosidic bonds.

entries.label: D-glucose
entries.definition: A glucose with <small>D</small>-configuration.

entries.label: vitamin B2
entries.definition: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called flavins that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>2</sub></small> deficiency. Symptoms associated with vitamin B<small><sub>2</sub></small> deficiency include glossitis, seborrhea, angular stomaitis, cheilosis and photophobia. The vitamers include riboflavin and its phosphate derivatives (and

entries.label: vitamin B3
entries.definition: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called pyridines that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B3 deficiency. Vitamin B3 deficiency causes a condition known as pellagra whose symptoms include depression, dermatitis and diarrhea.

entries.label: vitamin B5
entries.definition: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called pantothenic acids that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B5 deficiency. Deficiency of vitamin B5 is rare due to its widespread distribution in whole grain cereals, legumes and meat. Symptoms associated with vitamin B5 deficiency are difficult to asses since they are subtle and resemble those of other B

entries.label: vitamin B7
entries.definition: Any member of a group of vitamers that belong to the chemical structural class called biotins that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>7</sub></small> deficiency. Vitamin B<small><sub>7</sub></small> deficiency is very rare in individuals who take a normal balanced diet. Foods rich in biotin are egg yolk, liver, cereals, vegetables (spinach, mushrooms) and rice. Symptoms assoc

entries.label: vitamin B9
entries.definition: Any B-vitamin that exhibits biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>9</sub></small> deficiency. Vitamin B<small><sub>9</sub></small> refers to the many forms of folic acid and its derivatives, including tetrahydrofolic acid (the active form), methyltetrahydrofolate (the primary form found in blood), methenyltetrahydrofolate, folinic acid amongst others. They are present in abundance in gr

entries.label: vitamin B12
entries.definition: Any member of a group of cobalamin vitamers that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>12</sub></small> deficiency. Vitamin B<small><sub>12</sub></small> deficiency is associated with low red blood cell count and anemia. The vitamers are found in foods such as cereals, meat, fish, and poultry. The vitamers include adenosylcobalamin, hydroxocobalamin, cyanocobalamin, aquacobalami

entries.label: (R,R,S)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (R,R,S)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: (R,S,R)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (R,S,R)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: (R,S,S)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (R,S,S)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: (S,R,R)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (S,R,R)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: (S,S,R)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (S,S,R)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: (S,R,S)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (S,R,S)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: lactose
entries.definition: A glycosylglucose disaccharide, found most notably in milk, that consists of D-galactose and D-glucose fragments bonded through a beta-1->4 glycosidic linkage. The glucose fragment can be in either the alpha- or beta-pyranose form, whereas the galactose fragment can only have the beta-pyranose form.

entries.label: glycine betaine
entries.definition: The amino acid betaine derived from glycine.

entries.label: glycerol
entries.definition: A triol with a structure of propane substituted at positions 1, 2 and 3 by hydroxy groups.

entries.label: serine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is alanine substituted at position 3 by a hydroxy group.

entries.label: hydrogen chloride
entries.definition: A mononuclear parent hydride consisting of covalently bonded hydrogen and chlorine atoms.

entries.label: calcidiol
entries.definition: A hydroxycalciol that is calciol in which the hydrogen at position 25 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. A prehormone resulting from the oxidation of calciol in the liver, it is further hydroxylated in the kidney to give calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D3.

entries.label: benzyl alcohol
entries.definition: An aromatic alcohol that consists of benzene bearing a single hydroxymethyl substituent.

entries.label: sucrose
entries.definition: A glycosyl glycoside formed by glucose and fructose units joined by an acetal oxygen bridge from hemiacetal of glucose to the hemiketal of the fructose.

entries.label: fumaric acid
entries.definition: A butenedioic acid in which the C=C double bond has E geometry. It is an intermediate metabolite in the citric acid cycle.

entries.label: D-galacturonic acid
entries.definition: The D-enantiomer of galacturonic acid. It is the main component of pectin.

entries.label: phylloquinone
entries.definition: A member of the class of phylloquinones that consists of 1,4-naphthoquinone having methyl and phytyl groups at positions 2 and 3 respectively. The parent of the class of phylloquinones.

entries.label: hexose
entries.definition: Any six-carbon monosaccharide which in its linear form contains either an aldehyde group at position 1 (aldohexose) or a ketone group at position 2 (ketohexose).

entries.label: (R,R,R)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: An α-tocopherol that has R,R,R configuration. The naturally occurring stereoisomer of α-tocopherol, it is found particularly in sunflower and olive oils.

entries.label: polysaccharide
entries.definition: A biomacromolecule consisting of large numbers of monosaccharide residues linked glycosidically. This term is commonly used only for those containing more than ten monosaccharide residues.

entries.label: gamma-tocopherol
entries.definition: A tocopherol in which the chroman-6-ol core is substituted by methyl groups at positions 7 and 8. It is found particularly in maize (corn) oil and soya bean (soybean) oils.

entries.label: tyrosine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is phenylalanine bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 4 on the phenyl ring.

entries.label: citrulline
entries.definition: The parent compound of the citrulline class consisting of ornithine having a carbamoyl group at the N(5)-position.

entries.label: ammonium hydroxide
entries.definition: A solution of ammonia in water.

entries.label: xylose
entries.definition: An aldopentose, found in the embryos of most edible plants and used in medicine to test for malabsorption by administration in water to the patient.

entries.label: xyloglucan
entries.definition: A glucan that consists of a backbone of alpha-(1->4)-linked glucose residues, most of which are substituted with (1->6)-linked xylose side-chains.

entries.label: glutamic acid
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is glutaric acid bearing a single amino substituent at position 2.

entries.label: (1->4)-beta-D-glucan
entries.definition: A β-<small>D</small>-glucan in which the glucose units are connected by (1→4) linkages.

entries.label: ornithine
entries.definition: An alpha-amino acid that is pentanoic acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 5.

entries.label: L-fucose
entries.definition: Any form of fucose having L configuration.

entries.label: 6-O-alpha-D-glucopyranosyl-D-fructofuranose

aliases.norm: 6 o alpha d glucopyranosyl d fructofuranose

entries.definition: A glycosylfructose that is D-fructofuranose attached to a alpha-D-glucopyranosyl unit at position 6 via a glycosidic linkage. It is found in honey and sugarcane.

entries.label: xanthan
entries.definition: Xanthan gum is a polysaccharide produced by the bacteria Xanthomonas campestris. It is composed of pentasaccharide repeat units, comprising two glucose units, two mannose units, and one glucuronic acid unit. Its main chain consists of beta-D-glucose units linked at the 1 and 4 positions. Trisaccharide side chains contain a D-glucuronic acid unit between two D-mannose units linked at the O-3 positi

entries.label: acetamides
entries.definition: Compounds with the general formula RNHC(=O)CH<small><sub>3</sub></small>.

entries.label: aldaric acid
entries.definition: Dicarboxylic acids formed from aldoses by replacement of both terminal groups (CHO and CH<small><sub>2</sub></small>OH) by carboxy groups.

entries.label: aldonic acid
entries.definition: Any carbohydrate acid formed by oxidising the aldehyde functional group of an aldose to a carboxylic acid functional group. Aldonic acids have the general formula HOCH2[CH(OH)]nC(=O)OH.

entries.label: alkaloid
entries.definition: Any of the naturally occurring, basic nitrogen compounds (mostly heterocyclic) occurring mostly in the plant kingdom, but also found in bacteria, fungi, and animals. By extension, certain neutral compounds biogenetically related to basic alkaloids are also classed as alkaloids. Amino acids, peptides, proteins, nucleotides, nucleic acids, amino sugars and antibiotics are not normally regarded as al

entries.label: alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: A tocopherol that is chroman-6-ol substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 5, 7 and 8 and a 4,8,12-trimethyltridecyl group at position 2.

entries.label: arabinan
entries.definition: A polysaccharide composed of arabinose residues.

entries.label: asparagine
entries.definition: An alpha-amino acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to the alpha-carbon of glycine is substituted by a 2-amino-2-oxoethyl group.

entries.label: aspartic acid
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that consists of succinic acid bearing a single α-amino substituent

entries.label: benzenetriol
entries.definition: A triol in which three hydroxy groups are substituted onto a benzene ring.

entries.label: benzimidazoles
entries.definition: An organic heterocyclic compound containing a benzene ring fused to an imidazole ring.

entries.label: beta-D-glucoside
entries.definition: Any D-glucoside in which the anomeric centre has beta-configuration.

entries.label: branched-chain amino acid
entries.definition: Any  amino acid  in which the parent hydrocarbon chain has one or more alkyl substituents

entries.label: carotene
entries.definition: Hydrocarbon carotenoids.

entries.label: cholines
entries.definition: A quaternary ammonium ion based on the choline ion and its substituted derivatives thereof.

entries.label: cyclodextrin
entries.definition: A macrocycle composed of five or more D-glucopyranose units bonded via (1->4)-linkages.

entries.label: cysteine derivative
entries.definition: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of cysteine at the amino group, carboxy group, or thiol group, or from the replacement of any hydrogen of cysteine by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing cysteine residues.

entries.label: diazole
entries.definition: An azole that is either one of a pair of heterocyclic organic compounds comprising three carbon atoms and two nitrogen atoms arranged in a ring.

entries.label: diol
entries.definition: A compound that contains two hydroxy groups, generally assumed to be, but not necessarily, alcoholic. Aliphatic diols are also called glycols.

entries.label: glucooligosaccharide
entries.definition: An oligosaccharide comprised of glucose residues.

entries.label: glutamic acid derivative
entries.definition: An amino acid derivative resulting from reaction of glutamic acid at the amino group or either of the carboxy groups, or from the replacement of any hydrogen by a heteroatom. The definition normally excludes peptides containing glutamic acid residues.

entries.label: glycosyl glycoside
entries.definition: Any disaccharide in which the two monosaccharide components are connected by a glycosidic linkage between their anomeric centres.

entries.label: guanidines
entries.definition: Any organonitrogen compound containing a carbamimidamido (guanidino) group. Guanidines have the general structure (R<small><sup>1</small></sup>R<small><sup>2</small></sup>N)(R<small><sup>3</small></sup>R<small><sup>4</small></sup>N)C=N-R<small><sup>5</small></sup> and are related structurally to amidines and ureas.

entries.label: hydroxyproline
entries.definition: A proline derivative that is proline substituted by at least one hydroxy group.

entries.label: imidazoles
entries.definition: A five-membered organic heterocycle containing two nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3, or any of its derivatives; compounds containing an imidazole skeleton.

entries.label: indoles
entries.definition: Any compound containing an indole skeleton.

entries.label: isoleucine
entries.definition: A 2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid having either (2R,3R)- or (2S,3S)-configuration.

entries.label: ketoaldonic acid
entries.definition: Oxo carboxylic acids formally derived from aldonic acids by replacement of a secondary CHOH group by a carbonyl group.

entries.label: ketohexose
entries.definition: Any hexose containing a single ketone group.

entries.label: ketose
entries.definition: Ketonic parent sugars (polyhydroxy ketones H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)[CH(OH)]mH) and their intramolecular hemiketals.

entries.label: leucine
entries.definition: A branched-chain amino acid that consists of glycine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the α-carbon is substituted by an isobutyl group.

entries.label: linolenic acid
entries.definition: A two-membered subclass of octadecatrienoic acid comprising the (9Z,12Z,15Z)- and (6Z,9Z,12Z)-isomers. Linolenic acids are nutrients essential to the formation of prostaglandins and are also used in making paints and synthetic resins.

entries.label: agar
entries.definition: A complex mixture of polysaccharides extracted from species of red algae. Its two main components are agarose and agaropectin. Agarose is the component responsible for the high-strength gelling properties of agar, while agaropectin provides the viscous properties.

entries.label: lysine
entries.definition: A diamino acid that is caproic (hexanoic) acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 6.

entries.label: maltodextrin
entries.definition: A dextrin in which the D-glucose units are linked by alpha-(1->4) glycosidic bonds.

entries.label: monounsaturated fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid with one double or triple bond in the fatty acid chain and singly bonded carbon atoms in the rest of the chain. MUFAs have positive effects on the cardiovascular system, and in diabetes treatment.

entries.label: pyridinecarboxamide
entries.definition: A member of the class of pyridines that is a substituted pyridine in which at least one of the substituents is a carboxamide or N-substituted caraboxamide group.

entries.label: nitrites
entries.definition: Salts and esters of nitrous acid, HONO.

entries.label: nucleoside phosphate
entries.definition: A nucleobase-containing molecular entity that is a nucleoside in which one or more of the sugar hydroxy groups has been converted into a mono- or poly-phosphate. The term includes both nucleotides and non-nucleotide nucleoside phosphates.

entries.label: octadecatrienoic acid
entries.definition: Any trienoic fatty acid having eighteen carbons.

entries.label: oligopeptide
entries.definition: A peptide containing a relatively small number of amino acids.

entries.label: omega-3 fatty acid
entries.definition: A family of polyunsaturated fatty acids that have in common a final carbon-carbon double bond in the ω−3 position, i.e., the third bond from the methyl end of the fatty acid.

entries.label: pentitol
entries.definition: An alditol obtained by reduction of any pentose.

entries.label: peptide antibiotic
entries.definition: A chemically diverse class of peptides that exhibit antimicrobial properties.

entries.label: phosphoric acid
entries.definition: A phosphorus oxoacid that consists of one oxo and three hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central phosphorus atom.

entries.label: polar amino acid
entries.definition: Any amino acid whose side chain is capable of forming one or more hydrogen bonds.

entries.label: polyol
entries.definition: A compound that contains two or more hydroxy groups.

entries.label: polyphosphates
entries.definition: Any phosphate that is a salt or an ester of polyphosphoric acid or its chalcogen analogues.

entries.label: polyunsaturated fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing more than one double bond. Acids in this group are reported to have cardioprotective effects; and levels are lowered in chronic fatigue syndrome.

entries.label: porphyrins
entries.definition: Natural pigments containing a fundamental skeleton of four pyrrole nuclei united through the α-positions by four methine groups to form a macrocyclic structure.

entries.label: proline
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is pyrrolidine bearing a carboxy substituent at position 2.

entries.label: purine nucleotide
entries.definition: Any nucleotide that has a purine nucleobase.

entries.label: purine ribonucleotide
entries.definition: Any ribonucleotide that has a purine nucleobase.

entries.label: purines
entries.definition: A class of imidazopyrimidines that consists of purine and its substituted derivatives.

entries.label: pyridinemonocarboxylic acid
entries.definition: A monocarboxylic acid in which the carboxy group is attached to a pyridine (or substituted pyridine) ring.

entries.label: pyridines
entries.definition: Any organonitrogen heterocyclic compound based on a pyridine skeleton and its substituted derivatives.

entries.label: quinolines
entries.definition: A class of aromatic heterocyclic compounds each of which contains a benzene ring ortho fused to carbons 2 and 3 of a pyridine ring.

entries.label: rhamnose
entries.definition: A deoxymannose sugar that is the 6-deoxy derivative of hexose.

entries.label: saturated fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing no carbon to carbon multiple bonds. Known to produce adverse biological effects when ingested to excess.

entries.label: serine family amino acid
entries.definition: An α-amino acid which is biosynthesised from 3-phosphoglycerate (i.e. serine, glycine, cysteine and homocysteine). A closed class.

entries.label: short-chain fatty acid
entries.definition: An aliphatic monocarboxylic acid with a chain length of less than C<small><sub>6</sub></small>. If any non-hydrocarbon substituent is present, the compound is not normally regarded as a short-chain fatty acid.

entries.label: sialic acid
entries.definition: Any of the N-acylneuraminic acids and their esters and other derivatives of the alcoholic hydroxy groups.

entries.label: sodium hydrogensulfite
entries.definition: An inorganic sodium salt having hydrogensulfite as the counterion.

entries.label: sulfuric acid
entries.definition: A sulfur oxoacid that consists of two oxo and two hydroxy groups joined covalently to a central sulfur atom.

entries.label: tetrapyrrole
entries.definition: A natural pigment containing four pyrrole rings joined by one-carbon units linking position 2 of one pyrrole ring to position 5 of the next.

entries.label: vitamin B1
entries.definition: Any member of the group of 1,3-thiazolium cations that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>1</sub></small> deficiency in animals. Symptoms of vitamin B<small><sub>1</sub></small> deficiency include constipation, loss of apetite, fatigue, nausea, delirium, blurry vision and muscle weakness. Severe vitamin B<small><sub>1</sub></small> deficiency can also lead to a disease known

entries.label: threonine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to the α-carbon of glycine is substituted by a 1-hydroxyethyl group.

entries.label: tocopherol
entries.definition: A collective name for a group of closely related lipids that contain a chroman-6-ol nucleus substituted at position 2 by a methyl group and by a saturated hydrocarbon chain consisting of three isoprenoid units. They are designated as α-, β-, γ-, and δ-tocopherol depending on the number and position of additional methyl substituents on the aromatic ring. Tocopherols occur in vegetable oils and vege

entries.label: trehalose
entries.definition: A disaccharide formed by a (1<->1)-glycosidic bond between two units of D-glucose.

entries.label: triol
entries.definition: A chemical compound containing three hydroxy groups.

entries.label: tryptamines
entries.definition: Tryptamine and its substitution derivatives.

entries.label: unsaturated fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing at least one C=C or C≡C bond.

entries.label: valine
entries.definition: A branched-chain amino acid that consists of glycine in which one of the hydrogens attached to the α-carbon is substituted by an isopropyl group.

entries.label: vitamin D
entries.definition: Any member of a group of fat-soluble hydroxy seco-steroids that exhibit biological activity against vitamin D deficiency. Vitamin D  can be obtained from sun exposure, food and supplements and is biologically inactive and converted into the biologically active calcitriol via double hydroxylation in the body.

entries.label: vitamin B6
entries.definition: Any member of the group of pyridines that exhibit biological activity against vitamin B<small><sub>6</sub></small> deficiency. Vitamin B<small><sub>6</sub></small> deficiency is associated with microcytic anemia, electroencephalographic abnormalities, dermatitis with cheilosis (scaling on the lips and cracks at the corners of the mouth) and glossitis (swollen tongue), depression and confusion, and

entries.label: alpha-linolenic acid
entries.definition: A linolenic acid with cis-double bonds at positions 9, 12 and 15. Shown to have an antithrombotic effect.

entries.label: folic acid
entries.definition: An N-acyl-amino acid that is a form of the water-soluble vitamin B9. Its biologically active forms (tetrahydrofolate and others) are essential for nucleotide biosynthesis and homocysteine remethylation.

entries.label: cyanidin 3-O-beta-D-galactoside
entries.definition: An anthocyanin cation that is cyanidin(1+) carrying a single beta-D-galactosyl substituent at position 3.

entries.label: histidine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is propanoic acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2 and a 1H-imidazol-4-yl group at position 3.

entries.label: monensin A
entries.definition: A spiroketal, monensin A is the major component of monensin, a mixture of antibiotic substances produced by Streptomyces cinnamonensis. An antiprotozoal, it is used as the sodium salt as a feed additive for the prevention of coccidiosis in poultry and as a growth promoter in cattle.

entries.label: galactomannan
entries.definition: A heteroglycan consisting of a mannan backbone with galactose side groups.

entries.label: caffeine
entries.definition: A trimethylxanthine in which the three methyl groups are located at positions 1, 3, and 7. A purine alkaloid that occurs naturally in tea and coffee.

entries.label: myristoleic acid
entries.definition: A tetradecenoic acid in which the double bond is at the 9-10 position and has Z configuration. Myristoleic acid has been isolated from Serenoa repens and has cytotoxic and apoptosis-inducing effects.

entries.label: tryptophan
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is alanine bearing an indol-3-yl substituent at position 3.

entries.label: L-dehydroascorbic acid
entries.definition: Dehydroascorbic acid having the L-configuration.

entries.label: elaidic acid
entries.definition: A 9-octadecenoic acid and the trans-isomer of oleic acid.

entries.label: starch
entries.definition: The most important reserve polysaccharide found in plants. It is a glucan consisting of amylose and amylopectin.

entries.label: phenylalanine
entries.definition: An aromatic amino acid that is alanine in which one of the methyl hydrogens is substituted by a phenyl group.

entries.label: amylopectin
entries.definition: A polydisperse highly branched polysaccharide derivative composed of chains of D-glucopyranose residues in alpha(1->4) glycosidic linkage. The chains are joined together by alpha(1->6) glycosidic linkages. A small number of alpha(1->3) glycosidic linkages and some 6-phosphate ester groups also may occur. The branches in amylopectin typically contain 24 to 30 glucose residues.

entries.label: cyanidin 3-O-rutinoside
entries.definition: A rutinoside consisting of cyanidin having the rutinosyl group at the 3-position.

entries.label: amylose
entries.definition: A glucan composed of unbranched chains of D-glucopyranose residues in alpha(1->4) glycosidic linkage. The number of repeated glucose subunits (n) is usually in the range of 300 to 3000, but can be many thousands. One of the two components of starch (the other, 70-80%, being amylopectin). Cf. linear maltodextrin, in which the chain length is typically between 3 and 17 glucose units.

entries.label: theophylline
entries.definition: A dimethylxanthine having the two methyl groups located at positions 1 and 3. It is structurally similar to caffeine and is found in green and black tea.

entries.label: galactose
entries.definition: An aldohexose that is the C-4 epimer of glucose.

entries.label: glutamine
entries.definition: An alpha-amino acid that consists of butyric acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2 and a carbamoyl substituent at position 4.

entries.label: mescaline
entries.definition: A phenethylamine alkaloid that is phenethylamine substituted at positions 3, 4 and 5 by methoxy groups.

entries.label: vitamin K
entries.definition: Any member of a group of fat-soluble 2-methyl-1,4-napthoquinones that exhibit biological activity against vitamin K deficiency. Vitamin K is required for the synthesis of prothrombin and certain other blood coagulation factors.

entries.label: alpha-carotene
entries.definition: A cyclic carotene with a beta- and an epsilon-ring at opposite ends respectively.

entries.label: arabinoxylan
entries.definition: A member of the class of arabinoxylans that consists of a polymer chain of beta-(1->4)-linked D-xylopyranose units, many of which are 2- or 3-substituted, or 2,3-disubstituted by alpha-L-arabinofuranosyl residues.

entries.label: ajugose
entries.definition: A hexasaccharide that is verbascose which has an additional unit of alpha-D-galactopyranose attached by a 1->6 glycosidic linkage to the terminal galactosyl residue.

entries.label: verbascose
entries.definition: A pentasaccharide that is stachiose which has an additional unit of alpha-D-galactopyranose attached by a 1->6 glycosidic linkage to the terminal galactosyl residue.

entries.label: gamma-linolenic acid
entries.definition: A C18, omega-6 acid fatty acid comprising a linolenic acid having cis- double bonds at positions 6, 9 and 12.

entries.label: dextrin
entries.definition: Glucans produced by the hydrolysis of starch or glycogen. They are mixtures of polymers of <small>D</small>-glucose units linked by α(1→4) or α(1→6) glycosidic bonds.

entries.label: palmitoleic acid
entries.definition: A hexadec-9-enoic acid in which the double bond at position C-9 has cis configuration.

entries.label: fructose
entries.definition: A ketohexose that is an isomer of glucose.

entries.label: aspartame
entries.definition: A dipeptide obtained by formal condensation of the α-carboxy group of <small>L</small>-aspartic acid with the amino group of methyl <small>L</small>-phenylalaninate. Commonly used as an artificial sweetener.

entries.label: erucic acid
entries.definition: A docosenoic acid having a cis- double bond at C-13. It is found particularly in brassicas - it is a major component of mustard and rapeseed oils and is produced by broccoli, Brussels sprouts, kale, and wallflowers.

entries.label: fructan
entries.definition: Polysaccharides composed of fructose residues.

entries.label: piperine
entries.definition: A N-acylpiperidine that is piperidine substituted by a (1E,3E)-1-(1,3-benzodioxol-5-yl)-5-oxopenta-1,3-dien-5-yl group at the nitrogen atom. It is an alkaloid isolated from the plant Piper nigrum.

entries.label: icosanoic acid
entries.definition: A C20 striaght-chain saturated fatty acid which forms a minor constituent of peanut (L. arachis) and corn oils. Used as an organic thin film in the production of liquid crystals for a wide variety of technical applications.

entries.label: octanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain saturated fatty acid that is heptane in which one of the hydrogens of a terminal methyl group has been replaced by a carboxy group. Octanoic acid is also known as caprylic acid.

entries.label: octadecanoic acid
entries.definition: A C18 straight-chain saturated fatty acid component of many animal and vegetable lipids. As well as in the diet, it is used in hardening soaps, softening plastics and in making cosmetics, candles and  plastics.

entries.label: tetracosanoic acid
entries.definition: A C24 straight-chain saturated fatty acid.

entries.label: menadione
entries.definition: A member of the class of 1,4-naphthoquinones that is 1,4-naphthoquinone which is substituted at position 2 by a methyl group. It is used as a nutritional supplement and for the treatment of hypoprothrombinemia.

entries.label: tetradecanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain, fourteen-carbon, long-chain saturated fatty acid mostly found in milk fat.

entries.label: vitamin D2
entries.definition: A vitamin D supplement and has been isolated from alfalfa.

entries.label: calciol
entries.definition: A hydroxy seco-steroid that is (5Z,7E)-9,10-secocholesta-5,7,10(19)-triene in which the pro-S hydrogen at position 3 has been replaced by a hydroxy group. It is the inactive form of vitamin D3, being hydroxylated in the liver to calcidiol (25-hydroxyvitamin D3), which is then further hydroxylated in the kidney to give calcitriol (1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3), the active hormone.

entries.label: docosanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain, C22, long-chain saturated fatty acid.

entries.label: theobromine
entries.definition: A dimethylxanthine having the two methyl groups located at positions 3 and 7. A purine alkaloid derived from the cacao plant, it is found in chocolate, as well as in a number of other foods, and is a vasodilator, diuretic and heart stimulator.

entries.label: chlorophyll
entries.definition: A family of magnesium porphyrins, defined by the presence of a fifth ring beyond the four pyrrole-like rings. The rings can have various side chains which usually include a long phytol chain.

entries.label: arginine
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is glycine in which the α-is substituted by a 3-guanidinopropyl group.

entries.label: L-ascorbic acid
entries.definition: The L-enantiomer of ascorbic acid and conjugate acid of L-ascorbate.

entries.label: monocarboxylic acid amide
entries.definition: A carboxamide derived from a monocarboxylic acid.

entries.label: mannitol
entries.definition: A hexitol produced by a variety of organisms including bacteria, fungi, lichens and plants.

entries.label: beta-D-Gal-(1->3)-beta-D-GlcNAc-(1->3)-beta-D-Gal-(1->4)-D-Glc

aliases.norm: beta d gal 1 3 beta d glcnac 1 3 beta d gal 1 4 d glc

aliases.text: beta d gal beta d glcnac beta d gal d glc
aliases.norm: beta d gal beta d glcnac beta d gal d glc

entries.definition: A tetrasaccharide comprising residues of galactose, N-acetylglucosamine, galactose and glucose in a linear sequence, all joined by beta-linkages.

entries.label: isobutane
entries.definition: An alkane that is propane substituted by a methyl group at position 2.

entries.label: flavin
entries.definition: A derivative of the dimethylisoalloxazine (7,8-dimethylbenzo[g]pteridine-2,4(3H,10H)-dione) skeleton, with a substituent on the 10 position.

entries.label: silicon dioxide
entries.definition: A silicon oxide made up of linear triatomic molecules in which a silicon atom is covalently bonded to two oxygens.

entries.label: benzoic acid
entries.definition: A compound comprising a benzene ring core carrying a carboxylic acid substituent.

entries.label: propionic acid
entries.definition: A short-chain saturated fatty acid comprising ethane attached to the carbon of a carboxy group.

entries.label: citric acid
entries.definition: A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms.

entries.label: dodecanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain, twelve-carbon medium-chain saturated fatty acid with strong bactericidal properties; the main fatty acid in coconut oil and palm kernel oil.

entries.label: adipic acid
entries.definition: An α,ω-dicarboxylic acid that is the 1,4-dicarboxy derivative of butane.

entries.label: pyridoxine hydrochloride
entries.definition: The hydrochloride salt of pyridoxine.

entries.label: ammonium chloride
entries.definition: An inorganic chloride having ammonium as the counterion.

entries.label: calcium oxide
entries.definition: A member of the class of calcium oxides of calcium and oxygen in a 1:1 ratio.

entries.label: bixin
entries.definition: A carotenoic acid that is the 6'-monomethyl ester of 9'-cis-6,6'-diapocarotene-6,6'-dioic acid.

entries.label: magnesium carbonate
entries.definition: A magnesium salt with formula CMgO<small><sub>3</sub></small>. Its hydrated forms, particularly the di-, tri-, and tetrahydrates occur as minerals.

entries.label: methylparaben
entries.definition: A 4-hydroxybenzoate ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid with methanol. It is the most frequently used antimicrobial preservative in cosmetics. It occurs naturally in several fruits, particularly in blueberries.

entries.label: pelargonidin 3-O-rutinoside
entries.definition: An anthocyanin cation consisting of pelargonidin having a rutinosyl [6-deoxy-alpha-L-mannosyl-(1->6)-beta-D-glucosyl] residue attached at the 3-hydroxy position.

entries.label: potassium acetate
entries.definition: A potassium salt comprising equal numbers of potassium and acetate ions

entries.label: propylparaben
entries.definition: The benzoate ester that is the propyl ester of 4-hydroxybenzoic acid.   Preservative typically found in many water-based cosmetics, such as creams, lotions, shampoos and bath products. Also used as a food additive.

entries.label: saccharin
entries.definition: A 1,2-benzisothiazole having a keto-group at the 3-position and two oxo substituents at the 1-position. It is used as an artificial sweetening agent.

entries.label: sucralose
entries.definition: A disaccharide derivative consisting of 4-chloro-4-deoxy-α-<small>D</small>-galactopyranose and 1,6-dichloro-1,6-dideoxy-β-<small>D</small>-fructofuranose units linked by a glycosidic bond.

entries.label: titanium dioxide
entries.definition: A titanium oxide with the formula TiO<small><sub>2</sub></small>.  A naturally occurring oxide sourced from ilmenite, rutile and anatase, it has a wide range of applications.

entries.label: heptadecanoic acid
entries.definition: A C17 saturated fatty acid and trace component of fats in ruminants.

entries.label: all-cis-octadeca-6,9,12,15-tetraenoic acid
entries.definition: An octadecatetraenoic acid having four double bonds located at positions 6, 9, 12 and 15 (the all-cis-isomer). It has been isolated from Lithospermum officinale and fish oils.

entries.label: (11Z)-icos-11-enoic acid
entries.definition: An icosenoic acid having a cis- double bond at position 11.

entries.label: potassium chloride
entries.definition: A metal chloride salt with a K(+) counterion.

entries.label: amide
entries.definition: An amide is a derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

entries.label: calcium gluconate
entries.definition: The calcium salt of <small>D</small>-gluconic acid.

entries.label: calcium acetate
entries.definition: The calcium salt of acetic acid. It is used, commonly as a hydrate, to treat hyperphosphataemia (excess phosphate in the blood) in patients with kidney disease: the calcium ion combines with dietary phosphate to form (insoluble) calcium phosphate, which is excreted in the faeces.

entries.label: calcium carbonate
entries.definition: A calcium salt with formula CCaO<small><sub>3</sub></small>.

entries.label: vitamin E
entries.definition: Any member of a group of fat-soluble chromanols  that exhibit biological activity against vitamin E deficiency. The vitamers in this class consists of a chroman-6-ol core which is substituted at position 2 by a methyl group and (also at position 2) either a saturated or a triply-unsaturated hydrocarbon chain consisting of three isoprenoid units. The major function of vitamin E is to act as a natur

entries.label: tocotrienol
entries.definition: A tocol in which the hydrocarbon chain at position 2 contains three double bonds.

entries.label: vitamin D4
entries.definition: It is present in mushrooms.

entries.label: primary amide
entries.definition: A derivative of an oxoacid RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which an acidic hydroxy group has been replaced by an amino or substituted amino group.

entries.label: secondary amide
entries.definition: A derivative of two oxoacids RkE(=O)l(OH)m (l ≠ 0) in which two acyl groups are attached to the amino or substituted amino group.

entries.label: alpha-tocotrienol
entries.definition: A tocotrienol that is chroman-6-ol substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 5, 7 and 8 and a farnesyl chain at position 2. It has been found in palm oil derived from Elaeis guineensis.

entries.label: beta-tocotrienol
entries.definition: A tocotrienol that is chroman-6-ol substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 5 and 8 and a farnesyl chain at position 2. It has been isolated from various cultivars of wheat.

entries.label: delta-tocotrienol
entries.definition: A tocotrienol that is chroman-6-ol substituted by methyl groups at positions 2 and 8 and a farnesyl chain at position 2.

entries.label: gamma-tocotrienol
entries.definition: A tocotrienol that is chroman-6-ol substituted by methyl groups at positions 2, 7 and 8 and a farnesyl chain at position 2. A vitamin E family member that has potent anti-cancer properties against a wide-range of cancers.

entries.label: vitamin D5
entries.definition: A vitamin D in which the side-chain at position 17 consists of a (5R)-5-ethyl-6-methylheptan-2-yl group.

entries.label: canthaxanthin
entries.definition: A carotenone that consists of β,β-carotene bearing two oxo substituents at positions 4 and 4'.

entries.label: alpha-amino acid
entries.definition: An amino acid in which the amino group is located on the carbon atom at the position α to the carboxy group.

entries.label: amino acid
entries.definition: A carboxylic acid containing one or more amino groups.

entries.label: hexonic acid
entries.definition: Any aldonic acid formed by oxidising the aldehyde group of an aldohexose to a carboxylic acid group.

entries.label: aromatic amino acid
entries.definition: An amino acid whose structure includes an aromatic ring.

entries.label: aromatic amine
entries.definition: An amino compound in which the amino group is linked directly to an aromatic system.

entries.label: corrinoid
entries.definition: A derivative of the corrin nucleus, which contains four reduced or partly reduced pyrrole rings joined in a macrocycle by three =C‒ groups and one direct carbon-carbon bond linking α positions.

entries.label: aldohexose
entries.definition: A hexose with a (potential) aldehyde group at one end.

entries.label: ribose
entries.definition: Any aldopentose where the open-chain form has all the hydroxy groups on the same side in the Fischer projection. Occurrs in two enantiomeric forms, D- and L-ribose, of which only the former is found in nature.

entries.label: psicose
entries.definition: A ketohexose that is the C-3 epimer of fructose.

entries.label: fucose
entries.definition: Any deoxygalactose that is deoxygenated at the 6-position.

entries.label: 2,6-di-tert-butyl-4-methylphenol
entries.definition: A member of the class of phenols that is 4-methylphenol substituted by tert-butyl groups at positions 2 and 6.

entries.label: carrageenan
entries.definition: A family of sulfated polysaccharides extracted from red seaweeds. The name is derived from a common name of red algae Chondrus crispus, "carrageen moss" (Irish moss).

entries.label: cellodextrin
entries.definition: A dextrin of varying length (two or more glucose monomers) resulting from cellulolysis, the breakdown of cellulose.

entries.label: quaternary ammonium ion
entries.definition: A derivative of ammonium, NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>, in which all four of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with univalent (usually organyl) groups.

entries.label: ammonium ion derivative
entries.definition: A derivative of ammonium, NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>, in which one (or more) of the hydrogens bonded to the nitrogen have been replaced with univalent organyl groups. The substituting carbon of the organyl group must not itself be directly attached to a heteroatom (thereby excluding protonated amides, hemiaminals, etc).

entries.label: ammonium compound
entries.definition: Compounds (NH<small><sub>4</sub></small><small><sup>+</small></sup>)Y<small><sup>−</small></sup> and derivatives, in which one or more of the hydrogens bonded to nitrogen have been replaced with univalent groups.

entries.label: organonitrogen compound
entries.definition: Any heteroorganic entity containing at least one carbon-nitrogen bond.

entries.label: fatty acid
entries.definition: Any aliphatic monocarboxylic acid derived from or contained in esterified form in an animal or vegetable fat, oil or wax. Natural fatty acids commonly have a chain of 4 to 28 carbons (usually unbranched and even-numbered), which may be saturated or unsaturated. By extension, the term is sometimes used to embrace all acyclic aliphatic carboxylic acids.

entries.label: monosaccharide
entries.definition: Parent monosaccharides are polyhydroxy aldehydes H[CH(OH)]nC(=O)H or polyhydroxy ketones H-[CHOH]n-C(=O)[CHOH]m-H with three or more carbon atoms. The generic term 'monosaccharide' (as opposed to oligosaccharide or polysaccharide) denotes a single unit, without glycosidic connection to other such units. It includes aldoses, dialdoses, aldoketoses, ketoses and diketoses, as well as deoxy sugars, pr

entries.label: sorbic acid
entries.definition: A hexadienoic acid with double bonds at C-2 and C-4; it has four geometrical isomers, of which the trans,trans-form is naturally occurring.

entries.label: diamino acid
entries.definition: Any amino acid carrying two amino groups.

entries.label: docosahexaenoic acid
entries.definition: Any C22 polyunsaturated fatty acid containing six double bonds.

entries.label: icosapentaenoic acid
entries.definition: Any straight-chain, C20 polyunsaturated fatty acid having five C=C double bonds.

entries.label: omega-6 fatty acid
entries.definition: A family of polyunsaturated fatty acids that have in common a final carbon-carbon double bond in the n-6 position, i.e., the sixth bond from the methyl end of the fatty acid.

entries.label: vaccenic acid
entries.definition: An octadecenoic acid having a double bond at position 11; and which can occur in cis- or trans- configurations.

entries.label: pelargonidin 3-O-beta-D-glucoside chloride

aliases.norm: pelargonidin 3 o beta d glucoside chloride

entries.definition: A member of the class of anthocyanin chlorides that has pelargonidin 3-O-beta-D-glucoside as the cationic counterpart.

entries.label: disaccharide
entries.definition: A compound in which two monosaccharides are joined by a glycosidic bond.

entries.label: nucleotide
entries.definition: A nucleotide is a nucleoside phosphate resulting from the condensation of the 3 or 5 hydroxy group of a nucleoside with phosphoric acid.

entries.label: glucan
entries.definition: A polysaccharide composed of glucose residues.

entries.label: homopolysaccharide
entries.definition: Glycans composed of a single type of monosaccharide residue. They are named by replacing the ending '-ose' of the sugar by '-an'.

entries.label: galactan
entries.definition: Polysaccharides composed of galactose residues.

entries.label: xylan
entries.definition: Polysaccharides composed of xylose residues.

entries.label: folic acids
entries.definition: A group of heterocyclic compounds based on the pteroic acid skeleton conjugated with one or more <small>L</small>-glutamic acid units.

entries.label: gallate ester
entries.definition: A benzoate ester that is any ester resulting from the formal condensation of the carboxy group of gallic acid (3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoic acid) with an alcoholic or phenolic hydroxy group.

entries.label: carboxamide
entries.definition: An amide of a carboxylic acid, having the structure RC(=O)NR<small><sub>2</sub></small>. The term is used as a suffix in systematic name formation to denote the ‒C(=O)NH<small><sub>2</sub></small> group including its carbon atom.

entries.label: cyanidin 3-O-beta-D-galactoside chloride

aliases.norm: cyanidin 3 o beta d galactoside chloride

entries.definition: A memeber of the class of anthocyanin chlorides that has cyanidin 3-O-beta-D-galactoside  as the cationic counterpart.

entries.label: mannose
entries.definition: An aldohexose that is the C-2 epimer of glucose.

entries.label: mixed diacylamine
entries.definition: Any imide in which the acyl substituents are any two from carboacyl, sulfonyl and phosphoryl

entries.label: butane
entries.definition: A straight chain alkane composed of 4 carbon atoms.

entries.label: cyanin chloride
entries.definition: A member of the class of anthocyanin chlorides that has cyanin cation as the cationic counterpart.

entries.label: polypyrrole
entries.definition: A compound composed of two or more pyrrole units.

entries.label: organonitrogen heterocyclic compound
entries.definition: Any organonitrogen compound containing a cyclic component with nitrogen and at least one other element as ring member atoms.

entries.label: pyrrolidines
entries.definition: Any of a class of heterocyclic amines having a saturated five-membered ring.

entries.label: 2-amino-3-hydroxybutanoic acid
entries.definition: An α-amino acid that is butanoic acid substituted by an amino group at position 2 and a hydroxy group at position 3.

entries.label: 2-amino-3-methylpentanoic acid
entries.definition: A branched chain amino acid that consists of 3-methylpentanoic acid bearing an amino substituent at position 2.

entries.label: diazines
entries.definition: Any organic heterocyclic compound containing a benzene ring in which two of the C-H fragments have been replaced by isolobal nitrogens (the diazine parent structure).

entries.label: aminopyrimidine
entries.definition: A member of the class of  pyrimidines that is pyrimidine substituted by at least one amino group and its derivatives.

entries.label: anthocyanin
entries.definition: Any flavonoid that is a glycoside derivative of anthocyanidin. Anthocyanins are water-souluble plant pigments that generally occur as acidic salts exhibiting bright colours.

entries.label: anthocyanin chlorides
entries.definition: An organic chloride salt of any anthocyanin.

entries.label: tetramine
entries.definition: Any polyamine that contains four amino groups.

entries.label: straight-chain saturated fatty acid
entries.definition: Any saturated fatty acid lacking a side-chain.

entries.label: pyrimidines
entries.definition: Any compound having a pyrimidine as part of its structure.

entries.label: polyazaalkane
entries.definition: Any azaalkane in which two or more carbons in the chain are replaced by nitrogen.

entries.label: curcumin
entries.definition: A β-diketone that is methane in which two of the hydrogens are substituted by feruloyl groups. A natural dyestuff found in the root of Curcuma longa.

entries.label: D-hexose
entries.definition: A hexose that has <small>D</small>-configuration at position 5.

entries.label: (R)-lactic acid
entries.definition: An optically active form of lactic acid having (R)-configuration.

entries.label: EDTA(4-)
entries.definition: A tetracarboxylic acid anion formed by deprotonation of all four carboxy groups in ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA).

entries.label: (S)-lactic acid
entries.definition: An optically active form of lactic acid having (S)-configuration.

entries.label: pentadecanoic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain saturated fatty acid containing fifteen-carbon atoms.

entries.label: (15Z)-tetracosenoic acid
entries.definition: A tetracosenoic acid having a cis-double bond at position 15.

entries.label: thiabendazole
entries.definition: A member of the class of benzimidazoles carrying a 1,3-thiazol-4-yl substituent at position 2. A mainly post-harvest fungicide used to control a wide range of diseases including Aspergillus, Botrytis, Cladosporium and Fusarium.

entries.label: (S,S,S)-alpha-tocopherol
entries.definition: The (S,S,S)-stereoisomer of α-tocopherol.

entries.label: dipeptide
entries.definition: Any molecule that contains two amino-acid residues connected by peptide linkages.

entries.label: poly(ethylene glycol)
entries.definition: A polymer composed of repeating ethyleneoxy units.

entries.label: (R)-pantothenic acid
entries.definition: A pantothenic acid having R-configuration.

entries.label: beta-tocopherol
entries.definition: A tocopherol in which the chroman-6-ol core is substituted by methyl groups at positions 5 and 8. While it is found in low concentrations in many vegetable oils, only cottonseed oil contains significant amounts.

entries.label: delta-tocopherol
entries.definition: A tocopherol in which the chroman-6-ol core is substituted by a methyl group at position 8. It is found particularly in maize (corn) oil and soya bean (soybean) oils.

entries.label: butane-1,2,3,4-tetrol
entries.definition: A tetritol that is butane substituted by hydroxy groups at positions 1, 2, 3 and 4.

entries.label: heterocyclic fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing a ring composed of atoms including at least one heteroatom.

entries.label: thiazoles
entries.definition: An azole in which the five-membered heterocyclic aromatic skeleton contains a N atom and one S atom.

entries.label: thiamine hydrochloride
entries.definition: A hydrochloride obtained by combining thiamine chloride with one molar equivalent of hydrochloric acid.

entries.label: beta-cyclodextrin
entries.definition: A cyclodextrin composed of seven α-(1→4) linked <small>D</small>-glucopyranose units.

entries.label: organic amino compound
entries.definition: A compound formally derived from ammonia by replacing one, two or three hydrogen atoms by organyl groups.

entries.label: tetrasaccharide
entries.definition: An oligosaccharide comprising four monomeric monosaccharide units.

entries.label: retinol
entries.definition: A retinoid consisting of 3,7-dimethylnona-2,4,6,8-tetraen-1-ol substituted at position 9 by a 2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl group (geometry of the four exocyclic double bonds is not specified).

entries.label: oligosaccharide
entries.definition: A compound in which monosaccharide units are joined by glycosidic linkages. The term is commonly used to refer to a defined structure as opposed to a polymer of unspecified length or a homologous mixture. When the linkages are of other types the compounds are regarded as oligosaccharide analogues.

entries.label: nitrates
entries.definition: Salts or esters of nitric acid.

entries.label: N-acyl-amino acid
entries.definition: A carboxamide resulting from the formal condensation of a carboxylic acid with the amino group of an amino acid.

entries.label: biotins
entries.definition: Compounds containing a biotin (5-[(3aS,4S,6aR)-2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazol-4-yl]pentanoic acid) skeleton.

entries.label: gelatin
entries.definition: A mixture of peptides and proteins produced by partial hydrolysis of collagen extracted from the skin, bones, and connective tissues of animals such as domesticated cattle, chicken, pigs, and fish.

entries.label: poly(vinylpyrrolidone)
entries.definition: A vinyl polymer composed of repeating -CH2-CR- units where R is a 2-oxopyrrolidin-1-yl group.

entries.label: sodium citrate
entries.definition: The trisodium salt of citric acid.

entries.label: sodium alginate
entries.definition: A copolymer macromolecule composed of homopolymeric blocks of 1→4-linked homopolymeric blocks of 1→4-linked sodium β-<small>D</small>-mannuronate and sodium α-<small>L</small>-guluronate residues, covalently linked together in different sequences or blocks. The sodium salt of alginic acid.

entries.label: olefinic fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing at least one C=C double bond.

entries.label: polysorbate 40
entries.definition: A polymer composed of PEG-ylated sorbitan, where the total number of poly(ethylene glycol) units is 20 (w + x + y + z = 20) and a single terminal is capped by a palmitoyl group.

entries.label: polysorbate 20
entries.definition: A polymer composed of PEG-ylated sorbitan, where the total number of poly(ethylene glycol) units is 20 (w + x + y + z = 20) and a single terminal is capped by a dodecanoyl group.

entries.label: polysorbate 60
entries.definition: A polymer composed of PEG-ylated sorbitan, where the total number of poly(ethylene glycol) units is 20 (w + x + y + z = 20) and a single terminal is capped by a stearate group.

entries.label: polysorbate 80
entries.definition: A polymer composed of PEG-ylated sorbitan, where the total number of poly(ethylene glycol) units is 20 (w + x + y + z = 20) and a single terminal is capped by an oleoyl group.

entries.label: methyl cellulose
entries.definition: A (1→4)-β-<small>D</small>-glucan compound formed by methylating cellulose through exposure to NaOH/CH3Cl.

entries.label: all-cis-icosa-11,14,17-trienoic acid
entries.definition: An icosatrienoic acid having three cis- double bonds at positions 11, 14 and 17.

entries.label: all-cis-icosa-8,11,14-trienoic acid
entries.definition: An icosatrienoic acid having three cis double bonds at positions 8, 11 and 14.

entries.label: quinoline yellow
entries.definition: A quinoline derivative with a 1,3-dioxoindan-2-yl substituent at C-2.

entries.label: 1,2-benzisothiazole
entries.definition: A benzothiazole consisting of a benzene ring fused to an isothiazole.

entries.label: harman
entries.definition: An indole alkaloid fundamental parent with a structure of 9H-beta-carboline carrying a methyl substituent at C-1. It has been isolated from the bark of Sickingia rubra, Symplocus racemosa, Passiflora incarnata, Peganum harmala, Banisteriopsis caapi and Tribulus terrestris, as well as from tobacco smoke. It is a specific, reversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase A.

entries.label: humulone
entries.definition: An optically active cyclic ketone consisting of 3,5,6-trihydroxycyclohexa-2,4-dien-1-one bearing two 3-methylbut-2-en-1-yl substituents at positions 4 and 6 as well as a 3-methylbutanoyl group at the 2-position.

entries.label: straight-chain fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid whose skeletal carbon atoms form an unbranched open chain.

entries.label: cyclic fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid containing anywhere in its structure a ring of atoms.

entries.label: palmitelaidic acid
entries.definition: A straight-chain, monounsaturated, 16-carbon fatty acid with a trans-double bond at position C-9; the trans-isomer of palmitoleic acid and predominant trans-16:1 isomer in cheeses from goat and ewe milk. Major dietary sources are partly hydrogenated vegetable oils.

entries.label: essential fatty acid
entries.definition: Any member of the sub-set of polyunsaturated fatty acid for which there is an absolute dietary requirement.

entries.label: medium-chain fatty acid
entries.definition: Any fatty acid with a chain length of between C<small><sub>6</sub></small> and C<small><sub>12</sub></small>.

entries.label: patent blue V
entries.definition: An iminium ion that is a dark bluish synthetic dye used as a food colouring agent

entries.label: nucleobase-containing molecular entity
entries.definition: Any compound that has a nucleobase as a part.

entries.label: docosapentaenoic acid
entries.definition: Any straight-chain, C22 fatty acid having five C=C double bonds.

entries.label: hemicellulose
entries.definition: Hemicelluloses are polysaccharides in plant cell walls that have β-(1→4)-linked backbones with an equatorial configuration. Hemicelluloses include xyloglucans, xylans, mannans and glucomannans, and β-(1→3,1→4)-glucans.

entries.label: dimethicone polymer
entries.definition: A polydimethylsiloxane polymer, composed of dimethicone macromolecules.

entries.label: L-arabinofuranose
entries.definition: The five-membered ring form of L-arabinose.

entries.label: lecithin
entries.definition: A lipid-rich mixture containing glycerol, fatty acids, phosphoric acid and other components.

entries.label: 7,7',9,9'-tetra-cis-lycopene
entries.definition: An acyclic psi,psi-carotene having cis double bonds at C-7, -7', -9 and -9'.

entries.label: ammonium sulfate
entries.definition: An inorganic sulfate salt obtained by reaction of sulfuric acid with two equivalents of ammonia. A high-melting (decomposes above 280°C) white solid which is very soluble in water (70.6 g/100 g water at 0°C; 103.8 g/100 g water at 100°C), it is widely used as a fertilizer for alkaline soils.

entries.label: amorphous cellulose
entries.definition: A (1->4)-beta-D-glucan (cellulose) in amorphous form with a structure consisting of several hundred to over ten thousand D-glucose residues joined by beta(1->4) glycosidic linkages.

entries.label: crystalline cellulose
entries.definition: A (1→4)-β-<small>D</small>-glucan (cellulose) in crystalline form with a structure consisting of several hundred to over ten thousand <small>D</small>-glucose residues joined by β(1→4) glycosidic linkages.

entries.label: zinc acetate
entries.definition: An acetate salt in which the cationic component is zinc(2+).

entries.label: sodium nitrate
entries.definition: The inorganic nitrate salt of sodium.

entries.label: sodium L-tartrate
entries.definition: The organic sodium salt that is the disodium salt of L-tartaric acid.

entries.label: potassium L-tartrate
entries.definition: The potassium salt of <small>L</small>-tartaric acid.

entries.label: potassium sodium L-tartrate
entries.definition: The organic sodium and potassium salt of <small>L</small>-tartaric acid (mol ratio 1:1:1).

entries.label: potassium dihydrogen phosphate
entries.definition: A potassium salt in which dihydrogen phosphate(1−) is the counterion.

entries.label: triammonium citrate
entries.definition: A citrate salt in which all three carboxy groups are deprotonated and associated with ammonium ions as counter-cations.

entries.label: potassium nitrate
entries.definition: The inorganic nitrate salt of potassium.

entries.label: lactulose
entries.definition: A synthetic galactosylfructose disaccharide used in the treatment of constipation and hepatic encephalopathy.

entries.label: monosodium glutamate
entries.definition: An organic sodium salt that is the monosodium salt of glutamic acid.

entries.label: D-xylose
entries.definition: Any xylose with D-configuration.

entries.label: magnesium dichloride
entries.definition: A magnesium salt comprising of two chlorine atoms bound to a magnesium atom.

entries.label: malic acid
entries.definition: A 2-hydroxydicarboxylic acid that is succinic acid in which one of the hydrogens attached to a carbon is replaced by a hydroxy group.

entries.label: tetrahydrofolate

entries.definition: Any of the 23 α-amino acids that are precursors to proteins, and are incorporated into proteins during translation.
