entries.label: biscuit (hard) food product
entries.definition: In Commonwealth nations and Ireland, a biscuit is a small baked product that would be called either a "cookie" or a "cracker" in the United States and most of English-speaking Canada. entries.label: fowl food product
entries.definition: Fowl are birds belonging to one of two biological orders, namely the gamefowl or landfowl (Galliformes) and the waterfowl (Anseriformes). Studies of anatomical and molecular similarities suggest these two groups are close evolutionary relatives; together, they form the fowl clade which is scientifically known as Galloanserae (initially termed Galloanseri).

entries.label: neet fish food product

entries.label: persimmon food product
entries.definition: The persimmon (sometimes spelled persimon) is the edible fruit of a number of species of trees in the genus Diospyros. The most widely cultivated of these is the Asian or Japanese persimmon, Diospyros kaki.

entries.label: chard food product
entries.definition: A food product made from a chard plant cultivar.

entries.label: spice rub
entries.definition: Spice rub is any mixture of ground spices that is made for the purpose of being rubbed on raw food before the food is cooked. The spice rub forms a coating on the food. The food can be marinated in the spice rub for some time for the flavors to incorporate into the food or it can be cooked immediately after it is coated in the rub. The spice rub can be left on or partially removed before cooking.

entries.label: multi-component food
entries.definition: A food product consisting of food material derived from ingredients sourced from multiple organisms.

entries.label: ham food product
entries.definition: Ham is pork from a leg cut that has been preserved by wet or dry curing, with or without smoking.  As a processed meat, the term "ham" includes both whole cuts of meat and ones that have been mechanically formed.

entries.label: cocoa flavanol
entries.definition: A cocoa flavanol is a naturally occurring dietary flavonoid found in the cacao plant.

entries.label: tualag honey
entries.definition: Tualang honey is a multifloral jungle honey, produced by an Asian type of bee called Apis dorsata, in nests hanging from the high branches of tualang trees.

entries.label: smetana
entries.definition: Smetana is one of the names for a range of sour creams from Central and Eastern Europe. It is a dairy product produced by souring heavy cream. It is similar to crème fraîche (28% fat), but nowadays mainly sold with 9% to 36% milkfat content depending on the country. Its cooking properties are different from crème fraîche and the lighter sour creams sold in the US, which contain 12 to 16% butterfat

entries.label: Bosc pear (raw)
entries.definition: The Beurré Bosc or Bosc is a cultivar of the European Pear (Pyrus communis) from France or Belgium originally. Also known as the Kaiser , it is grown in Europe, Australia, British Columbia and Ontario, Canada, and the northwestern U.S. states of California, Washington, and Oregon;

entries.label: burrito
entries.definition: A burrito is a dish in Mexican and Tex-Mex cuisine that consists of a flour tortilla with various other ingredients.

entries.label: blueberry juice
entries.definition: A fruit juice made primarily from blueberres.

entries.label: blue corn mush (dish)
entries.definition: Blue corn mush is a dish prepared by thickening blue corn meal, water, and juniper ash on the stove.

entries.label: blue corn meal
entries.definition: Blue corn meal is a corn meal that is ground from whole blue corn and has a sweet flavor. It is also a staple of New Mexican cuisine used commonly to make tortillas.

entries.label: carrot cake
entries.definition: Carrot cake is a cake that contains carrots mixed into the batter.

entries.label: gravlax
entries.definition: Gravlax is a Nordic dish consisting of raw salmon, cured in salt, sugar, and dill.

entries.label: O's cereal

entries.label: hoisin sauce
entries.definition: Hoisin sauce is a thick, fragrant sauce commonly used in Chinese cuisine as a glaze for meat, an addition to stir fries, or as dipping sauce.

entries.label: piadina flat bread
entries.definition: Piadina or Piada is a thin Italian flatbread, typically prepared in the Romagna historical region (Forlì, Cesena, Ravenna and Rimini).

entries.label: shish kebab
entries.definition: Shish kebab is a popular meal of skewered and grilled cubes of meat.

entries.label: masa
entries.definition: Masa is a corn dough or flour (masa harina) that has been soaked and cooked in an alkaline solution in the nixtamalization process. It is used for making corn tortillas, tamales, pupusas, and many other Latin American dishes.

entries.label: mulligatawny
entries.definition: Mulligatawny is an English soup which originated from South Indian cuisine.

entries.label: naan
entries.definition: Naan is a leavened, oven-baked flatbread found in the cuisines mainly of West Asia, Central Asia, Southeast Asia, the Indian subcontinent and the Caribbean.

entries.label: nachos
entries.definition: Nachos is a Mexican dish from northern Mexico that consists of heated tortilla chips or totopos covered with melted cheese (or a cheese-based sauce), often served as a snack or appetizer.

entries.label: ossobuco
entries.definition: Ossobuco is a specialty of Lombard cuisine of cross-cut veal shanks braised with vegetables, white wine and broth.

entries.label: pain au chocolat
entries.definition: Pain au chocolat, literally chocolate bread; also known as chocolatine in the south-west part of France and in Canada, is a type of viennoiserie sweet roll consisting of a cuboid-shaped piece of yeast-leavened laminated dough, similar in texture to a puff pastry, with one or two pieces of dark chocolate in the centre.

entries.label: potato waffle
entries.definition: A potato waffle is a potato-based savoury dish in a waffle shape.

entries.label: potato wedges
entries.definition: Potato wedges are wedges of potatoes, often large and unpeeled, that are either baked or fried.

entries.label: quesadilla
entries.definition: A quesadilla, or sometimes specifically a cheese quesadilla, is a Mexican dish, consisting of a tortilla that is filled primarily with cheese, and sometimes meats, beans, vegetables, and spices, and then cooked on a griddle.

entries.label: muscovado
entries.definition: Muscovado is a type of partially refined to unrefined sugar with a strong molasses content and flavour.

entries.label: añejo cheese
entries.definition: Añejo cheese is a firm, aged Mexican chees traditionally made from skimmed goat's milk, but most often available made from skimmed cow's milk.

entries.label: quesa chihuahua
entries.definition: In Mexico, queso Chihuahua is commonly recognized as a soft white cheese available in braids, balls or rounds and originates in the Mexican state of Chihuahua. In Chihuahua, it is called queso menonita, after the Mennonite communities of northern Mexico that first produced it.

entries.label: cotija cheese
entries.definition: Cotija is a cow's milk hard cheese that originated in Mexico. It is named after the town of Cotija, Michoacán.

entries.label: oaxaca cheese
entries.definition: Oaxaca cheese, more commonly referred to as Quesillo is a white, semihard cheese from Mexico, similar to unaged Monterey jack, but with a mozzarella-like string cheese texture.

entries.label: samosa
entries.definition: A samosa is a fried or baked dish with a savoury filling, such as spiced potatoes, onions, peas, or lentils.

entries.label: serrano ham
entries.definition: Serrano ham, or "Jamón serrano" in spanish, literally "ham from the sierra, or mountain range") is a type of dry-cured Spanish jamón (ham) which includes most varieties other than those made with black Iberian pigs (jamón ibérico).

entries.label: Iberian ham
entries.definition: Iberian ham, is a type of cured ham produced in Spain and Portugal. According to Spain's denominación de origen rules on food products, jamón ibérico may be made from black Iberian pigs, or cross-bred pigs so long as they are at least 50% ibérico.

entries.label: shell bean
entries.definition: Shell, shelled, or shelling beans are beans removed from their pods before being cooked or dried. Common beans can be used as shell beans, but the term also refers to other species of beans whose pods are not typically eaten, such as lima beans, soybeans, peas, and fava beans.

entries.label: tikka masala sauce
entries.definition: Tikka Masala (as sold in bottles in the UK) is a roasted and ground combination of common Indian spices, along with fried ginger paste, mixed into a gravy of cream and tomato puree.

entries.label: chicken tikki masala
entries.definition: Chicken tikka masala is a dish of chunks of roasted marinated chicken (chicken tikka) in a spiced curry sauce. The sauce is usually creamy and orange-coloured.

entries.label: tostada (tortilla)
entries.definition: Tostada is the name of various Mexican and Latin American dishes which features a flat or bowl-shaped (like a bread bowl) tortilla that is deep fried or toasted.

entries.label: triple sec
entries.definition: Triple sec, originally Curaçao triple sec, is a type of strong, sweet and colorless orange-flavored liqueur.

entries.label: triticale food product
entries.definition: Triticale is a hybrid of wheat (Triticum) and rye (Secale) first bred in laboratories during the late 19th century in Scotland and Germany.  Commercially available triticale is almost always a second-generation hybrid, i.e., a cross between two kinds of primary (first-cross) triticales.

entries.label: triticale flour
entries.definition: Triticale flour is flour made from triticale grain.

entries.label: tzimbalo melon pear
entries.definition: Tzimbalo pear fruit is a berry from the cultivated Solanum caripense evergreen shrub, a species native to South America.

entries.label: wagyu steak
entries.definition: Wagyu steak is steak cut from any of the four wagyu cattle varieties.

entries.label: black pudding
entries.definition: Black pudding is a type of blood sausage originating in Great Britain and Ireland. It is made from pork blood, with pork fat or beef suet, and a cereal, usually oatmeal, oat groats or barley groats. The high proportion of cereal, along with the use of certain herbs such as pennyroyal, serves to distinguish black pudding from blood sausages eaten in other parts of the world.

entries.label: wonton (filled)
entries.definition: A wonton (also spelled wantan, or wuntun in transliteration from Cantonese; Mandarin: húntun) is a type of Chinese dumpling commonly found across regional styles of Chinese cuisine.

entries.label: Red Delicious apple
entries.definition: A pome fruit of a Red Deliciousapple tree cultivar.

entries.label: blini
entries.definition: A blini is a Russian and Ukrainian pancake traditionally made from wheat or (more rarely) buckwheat flour and served with smetana, tvorog, butter, caviar and other garnishes.

entries.label: chocolate brownie
entries.definition: A chocolate brownie (commonly referred to as simply brownie) is a square, baked, chocolate dessert.

entries.label: chipotle
entries.definition: A chipotle is a smoke-dried ripe jalapeño chili pepper used for seasoning.

entries.label: chowder
entries.definition: Chowder is a type of soup or stew often prepared with milk or cream and thickened with broken crackers, crushed ship biscuit, or a roux. Variations of chowder can be seafood or vegetable.

entries.label: elderflower
entries.definition: Elderflower is the flower (blossom) of an elderberry plant

entries.label: focaccia
entries.definition: Focaccia is a flat oven-baked Italian bread product similar in style and texture to pizza dough.

entries.label: frog leg
entries.definition: A whole leg that is obtained from a frog.

entries.label: grape seed
entries.definition: Grapeseed refers to the seeds of grapes, from which oil can be extracted

entries.label: hibiscus tea (dry)
entries.definition: Hibiscus tea is a herbal tea made as an infusion from crimson or deep magenta-colored calyces (sepals) of the roselle (Hibiscus sabdariffa) flower. It is consumed both hot and cold. It has a tart, cranberry-like flavor.

entries.label: pork loin
entries.definition: A cut of meat from a pig, that comes from the tissue along the dorsal side of the rib cage.

entries.label: squash flower
entries.definition: Squash blossoms are the edible flowers of Cucurbita species, particularly Cucurbita pepo, the species that produces zucchini (courgette), marrow, spaghetti squash, and many other types of squash.

entries.label: Arborio rice
entries.definition: An Italian short-grain rice.

entries.label: bean sprout
entries.definition: A bean sprout is a germinated bean to be eaten raw or cooked.

entries.label: wine by region
entries.definition: A grape wine distinguished by the region its grapes were grown in.

entries.label: white grape (raw)
entries.definition: White grapes are actually green in color, and are evolutionarily derived from the purple grape.

entries.label: kava food product
entries.definition: Kava or kava kava or Piper methysticum (Latin "pepper" and Latinized Greek "intoxicating") is a crop of the Pacific Islands.  Kava is consumed throughout the Pacific Ocean cultures of Polynesia, including Hawaii and Vanuatu, and Melanesia and some parts of Micronesia for its sedating effects.

entries.label: Chardonnay wine
entries.definition: Chardonnay wine is wine produced using only Chardonnay grapes.

entries.label: Cabernet Sauvignon wine
entries.definition: A Cabernet Sauvignon wine is any wine produced using only Cabernet Sauvignon grapes. It often appears with Merlot and Cabernet Franc in blended Bordeaux wines.

entries.label: Chenin blanc wine
entries.definition: A Chenin blanc wine is any wine produced using only Chenin blanc grapes.

entries.label: Malbec wine
entries.definition: A Malbec wine is any wine produced using only Malbec grapes.

entries.label: Merlot wine
entries.definition: A Merlot wine is any wine produced using only Merlot grapes.

entries.label: Pinot blanc wine
entries.definition: A pinot blanc wine is any wine produced using only Pinco blanc grapes.

entries.label: Pinot gris wine
entries.definition: Pinot gris is a white wine varietal produced only from Pinot gris grapes.  The Italian synonym, Pinot Grigio, has become strongly associated with lighter wines produced in great quantities, particularly in northern Italy.

entries.label: Pinot noir wine
entries.definition: Pinot noir wine is a red wine varietal made only from Pinot noir grapes.  The thin skins and low levels of phenolic compounds lends pinot to producing mostly lightly colored, medium-bodied and low-tannin wines that can often go through phases of uneven and unpredictable aging.

entries.label: Pinotage wine
entries.definition: Pinotage wine is a red wine varietal produced only from Pinotage grapes. This type of wine can range from a fairly cheap, light-bodied red wine with some funky aromas (including extremes such as acetone, paint, rubber, and at times banana) all the way to full-bodied red wines with balance, elegance, fully developed black fruit flavors, and an enduring, sweet, smokey finish.

entries.label: Reserve wine
entries.definition: Reserve wine is wine of a higher quality than usual, or a wine that has been aged before being sold, or both. Traditionally, winemakers would reserve some of their best wine rather than sell it immediately, coining the term.

entries.label: Riesling wine
entries.definition: Riesling wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Riesling grapes, and offered as dry, semi-sweet, sweet, and sparkling white wines. Riesling wines are usually varietally pure and are seldom oaked.

entries.label: Sangiovese wine
entries.definition: Sangiovese wine is a red wine varietal produced only from Sangiovese grapes. It is prized for its high acid, firm tannins and balanced nature. Savory flavors of dark cherries and black stonefruit are characteristic, and may be backed by secondary notes of tomato leaf and dried herbs.

entries.label: Sauvignon blanc wine
entries.definition: Sauvignon blanc wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Sauvignon blanc grapes.  Its primary fruit flavors are lime, green apple, passion fruit and white peach. Depending on how ripe the grapes are when the wine is made, the flavor will range from zesty lime to flowery peach.

entries.label: Semillon wine
entries.definition: Semillon wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Semillon grapes.  The primary fruit flavors in Semillon wine are lemon, apple, pear and green papaya. Semillon is France’s 3rd most planted white wine variety behind Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay.

entries.label: Glera wine
entries.definition: Glera wine is a white wine varietal produced only from Glera grapes.

entries.label: Prosecco wine
entries.definition: Prosecco is an Italian white wine varietal produced primarily from Glera grapes, but other grape varieties may be included. Prosecco controlled designation of origin can be spumante ("sparkling wine"), frizzante ("semi-sparkling wine"), or tranquillo ("still wine").

entries.label: Syrah wine
entries.definition: Syrah wine is a white wine produced entirely from Syrah grapes.  The wines are often powerfully flavoured and full-bodied.

entries.label: Tempranillo wine
entries.definition: Tempranillo wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Tempranillo grapes.

entries.label: Zinfandel wine
entries.definition: Zinfandel wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Zinfandel grapes.  A classic wine is high in both alcohol and tannins, intensely flavored and deeply colored.

entries.label: Frappato wine
entries.definition: Frappato wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Frappato grapes.  As a varietal, Frappato produces light bodied wines with a distinct grapey aroma.

entries.label: Gamay noir wine
entries.definition: Gamay noir wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Gamay grapes.

entries.label: Gewürztraminer wine
entries.definition: Gewürztraminerwine is a white wine varietal produced entirely from Gewürztraminer grapes.

entries.label: Carignane wine
entries.definition: Carignane wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Carignane grapes.

entries.label: Grenache wine
entries.definition: Grenache wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Grenache grapes.

entries.label: Barbera wine
entries.definition: Barbera wine is a red wine varietal produced entirely from Barbera grapes.

entries.label: tagliatelle
entries.definition: Tagliatelle is a traditional type of egg pasta from the Emilia-Romagna and Marche regions of Italy. Individual pieces of tagliatelle are long, flat ribbons that are similar in shape to fettuccine and are typically about 6.5 to 10 mm (0.26 to 0.39 in) wide.

entries.label: tortellini
entries.definition: Tortellini are ring-shaped pasta, sometimes also described as "navel shaped", hence their alternative name of "belly button" (ombelico). They are typically stuffed with a mix of meat (pork loin, raw prosciutto, Mortadella), and Parmigiano Reggiano cheese.

entries.label: tortelloni
entries.definition: Tortelloni are stuffed pasta, the same shape as tortellini, but larger. They are usually stuffed with ricotta cheese and leaf vegetables, such as spinach.

entries.label: tortiglioni
entries.definition: Tortiglioni are a type of pasta, similar to rigatoni but larger and with deeper grooves which spiral around the pasta.

entries.label: fusilli
entries.definition: Fusilli are a variety of pasta that are formed into corkscrew or helical shapes. The word fusilli presumably comes from fuso ("spindle"), as traditionally it is "spun" by pressing and rolling a small rod over the thin strips of pasta to wind them around it in a corkscrew shape.

entries.label: conchiglie
entries.definition: Conchiglie, commonly known as "shells" or "seashells" is a type of pasta. It is usually sold in the plain durum wheat variety. The shell shape of the pasta allows the sauce to adhere to it.

entries.label: linguine
entries.definition: Linguine is a type of pasta similar to fettuccine and trenette but elliptical in section rather than flat. It is about 4 millimetres in width, which is wider than spaghetti but not as wide as fettuccine.

entries.label: penne
entries.definition: Penne is an extruded type of pasta with cylinder-shaped pieces, their ends cut at a bias. It is lexically related to Latin penna (meaning "feather" or "quill"), and was originally intended to imitate the then-ubiquitous fountain pen's steel nibs.

entries.label: Zakynthos wine
entries.definition: Zakynthos Wine is wine produced on the Greek island of Zakynthos (Zante) in the Ionian Sea. A wide array of native Ionian grape varieties have been planted on the island for centuries, and are most famously used to make the intensely flavored, highly acidic Verdea wine.

entries.label: Bordeaux wine
entries.definition: Any wine produced in the Bordeaux region of southwest France.

entries.definition: Food material which has been colored.

entries.definition: A food product traditionally consumed during supper.

entries.definition: A lipid food product is a food product made primarily of plant or animal fat or oil

entries.label: quick bread
entries.definition: Quick bread is any bread leavened with leavening agents other than yeast or eggs.

entries.label: almond bark
entries.definition: Almond bark (also known as vanilla flavored candy coating) is a chocolate-like confection made with vegetable fats instead of cocoa butter and with coloring and flavors added

entries.label: allspice
entries.definition: Allspice is the dried unripe fruit (berries, used as a spice) of Pimenta dioica, a midcanopy tree native to the Greater Antilles, southern Mexico, and Central America, now cultivated in many warm parts of the world.

entries.label: anchovy fillet
entries.definition: An anchovy fillet is a fish fillet taken from an anchovy fish.

entries.label: alfalfa sprout
entries.definition: A sprout from an alfalfa seed.

entries.label: chicken nugget
entries.definition: A chicken nugget is a chicken product made from chicken meat that is breaded or battered, then deep-fried or baked.

entries.label: chicken wing
entries.definition: A whole wing that is obtained from a chicken.

entries.label: Buffalo wing (dish)
entries.definition: Buffalo wings, invented in Buffalo, New York, are chicken wings that are generally deep-fried then coated or dipped in a sauce.

entries.label: cod liver food product
entries.definition: The liver of a cod fish

entries.label: crab claw
entries.definition: The claw of a crab

entries.label: fish cake
entries.definition:
A fishcake (sometimes written as fish cake) is a food item similar to a croquette, consisting of filleted fish or other seafood with potato patty, sometimes coated in breadcrumbs or batter, and fried.

Fishcakes as defined in the Oxford Dictionary of Food and Nutrition are chopped or minced fish mixed with potato, egg and flour with seasonings of onions, peppers and sometimes herbs.

entries.label: fish fillet
entries.definition: A fish fillet, from the French word filet meaning a thread or strip, is the flesh of a fish which has been cut or sliced away from the bone by cutting lengthwise along one side of the fish parallel to the backbone.

entries.label: pet food
entries.definition: Pet food is plant or animal material intended for consumption by pets.

entries.label: mixed vegetables
entries.definition: A mixture of at least two different vegetables.

entries.label: mustard greens
entries.definition: Mustard greens are leaves from a mustard plant

entries.label: navy bean
entries.definition: A white colored seed of a navy bean plant which is a varietal of a common bean plant (Phaseolus vulgaris)

entries.label: spiny lobster
entries.definition: Spiny lobsters, also known as langustas, langouste, or rock lobsters, are a family (Palinuridae) of about 60 species of achelate crustaceans, in the Decapoda Reptantia. Spiny lobsters are also, especially in Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, South Africa, and the Bahamas, called crayfish, sea crayfish, or crawfish ("kreef" in South Africa), terms which elsewhere are reserved for freshwater crayfish

entries.label: romaine lettuce head
entries.definition: A rosette of a romaine lettuce plant (Lactuca sativa var. longifolia).

entries.label: tropical fruit food product
entries.definition: A tropical fruit food product is any fruit product derived from a tropical or subtropical fruit producing plant.

entries.label: turkey breast
entries.definition: A whole breast that is obtained from a turkey.

entries.label: moth bean food product
entries.definition: A moth bean food product is a food product derived from the moth bean plant.

entries.label: canola meal
entries.definition: Canola meal is an oilseed meal made from canola grain.  Canola meal is a by-product of the oil crushing process.

entries.label: scallion food product
entries.definition: Scallions (also known as green onions, spring onions, or salad onions) are vegetables of various Allium onion species.

entries.label: alpaca meat food product
entries.definition: An Alpaca meat food product is a meat food product derived from an alpaca

entries.label: apple snail
entries.definition: Ampullariidae, common name the apple snails, is a family of large freshwater snails, aquatic gastropod mollusks with a gill and an operculum.

entries.definition: A whole breast that is obtained from a chicken.

entries.definition: Food material which has undergone a cleaning process.

entries.label: beef lung (raw)
entries.definition: A raw lung that is obtained from a beef.

entries.label: cracker
entries.definition: A cracker is a flat, dry baked food typically made with flour. In UK English, crackers are sometimes called water biscuits, savoury biscuits or biscuits.

entries.label: dog treat
entries.definition: Dog treat is a category of dog food that encompasses dog biscuits but can also include other chewy food materials like rawhide or bone.

entries.label: food (ground)
entries.definition: Comminuted material which has a ground characteristic.

entries.label: turkey meat (ground or minced)
entries.definition: A food product made of ground or minced turkey meat

entries.label: herring fillet
entries.definition: A herring fillet is a fillet cut of herring

entries.label: chicken drumstick
entries.definition: A whole drumstick that is obtained from a chicken.

entries.definition: Food material which has been dehulled.

entries.label: nutritional powder
entries.definition: A nutritional preparation in powdered form.

entries.label: Kielbasa
entries.definition: Kielbasa (from Polish kiełbasa)[a] is any type of meat sausage from Poland, and a staple of Polish cuisine.

entries.label: pork sausage
entries.definition: Pork sausage is sausage made with pork meat.

entries.label: turkey liver
entries.definition: A whole animal liver that is obtained from a turkey.

entries.label: snapper fillet
entries.definition: A fillet cut of a snapper fish

entries.label: food (seasoned)
entries.definition: Food material which has had seasoning applied to it.

entries.label: roast beef
entries.definition: Roast beef is a dish of beef which is roasted. Essentially prepared as a main meal, the leftovers are often used in sandwiches and sometimes are used to make hash.

entries.label: bird's eye chili
entries.definition: Bird's eye chili is a chili pepper, a variety from the species Capsicum annuum, commonly found in Ethiopia and across Southeast Asia.

entries.label: beef hamburger (dish)
entries.definition: A hamburger (short: burger) is a sandwich consisting of one or more cooked patties of ground meat, usually beef, placed inside a sliced bread roll or bun. The patty may be pan fried, grilled, or flame broiled.

entries.label: meat and bone meal
entries.definition: Meat and bone meal (MBM) is a product of the rendering industry. It is typically about 48–52% protein, 33–35% ash, 8–12% fat, and 4–7% water. It is primarily used in the formulation of animal feed to improve the amino acid profile of the feed.

entries.label: food (packaged)
entries.definition: Food material that has been placed in a container.

entries.label: Poultry by-product meal (PBM)
entries.definition: A high-protein commodity used as a major component in some pet foods. It is made from grinding clean, rendered parts of poultry carcasses and can contain bones, offal and undeveloped eggs, but only contains feathers that are unavoidable in the processing of the poultry parts.

entries.label: tuna fillet
entries.definition: A fillet cut of a tuna fish.

entries.label: roll or bun
entries.definition: A roll is a small, often round loaf of bread served as a meal accompaniment (eaten plain or with butter).  A bun is a small, sometimes sweet, bread, or bread roll.

entries.label: food (roasted)
entries.definition: Food material which has been roasted.

aliases.text: Soft-shell crab is a culinary term for crabs that have recently molted their old exoskeleton and are still soft. Soft-shells are removed from the water as soon as they molt to prevent any hardening of their shell. This means that almost the entire animal can be eaten, rather than having to shell the animal to reach the meat.

entries.label: guajillo chili food product
entries.definition: A guajillo chili or guajillo chile is a variety of chile pepper of the species *Capsicum annuum* which is widely used in the cuisine of Mexico. Its heat (rating 2,500 to 5,000 on the Scoville scale) is considered mild to medium.

entries.label: brown bean
entries.definition: The brown bean is chestnut brown colored bean with a small white-eye which originates in Scandanavia.

entries.label: marrow bean
entries.definition: A seed of a marrow bean plant which is a varietal of a common bean plant (Phaseolus vulgaris).

entries.label: velvet bean
entries.definition: A seed of a  velvet bean plant (Mucuna pruriens)

entries.label: vetch seed
entries.definition: A seed of a vetch plant.

entries.label: potato (whole or pieces)
entries.definition: A potato substance is a whole potato transformed into some derivative food material. It doesn't include potato food products that are ready to consume or simply require thawing or reheating.

entries.label: chicken egg (boiled)
entries.definition: A chicken egg which has been boiled, but may be hard boiled or soft boiled, and may have its shell on or off.

entries.label: goose egg (shell on, raw)
entries.definition: A raw goose egg in its shell.

entries.label: turkey egg (shell on, raw)
entries.definition: A raw turkey egg in its shell.

entries.label: banana powder
entries.definition: Banana powder is a powder made from processed bananas. It is used as a component for production of milk shakes and baby foods. It is also used in the manufacture of various types of cakes and biscuits.

entries.label: snow pea pod (edible, fresh)
entries.definition: A snow pea pod is a pea pod from a snow pea plant.

entries.label: turkey carcass (butchered, raw)
entries.definition: A whole turkey food product consists of the plucked carcass of a turkey with head and entrails removed and with organ meats and neck severed and possibly included in body cavity.

entries.label: olive oil (extra-virgin)
entries.definition: Extra virgin olive oil is a virgin olive oil which has a free acidity, expressed as oleic acid, of not more than 0.8 grams per 100 grams.

entries.label: edamame
entries.definition: Edamame is a preparation of immature soybeans in their pods, or with the pod removed. It originates in East Asia cuisine. The pods or beans are boiled or steamed and may be served with salt.

entries.label: edible bean pod
entries.definition: A bean pod which is still tender rather than one that has reached full maturity.

entries.definition: A liver food product is a food product that derives from one or more liver organs.

entries.label: kidney food product
entries.definition: A food product that derives from one or more kidney organs

entries.label: lung food product
entries.definition: A lung food product is a food product that derivers from one or more mammalian lungs.

entries.definition: A raw lung that is obtained from a sheep.

entries.definition: A whole raw lung is a whole lung organ obtained from an animal during a butchery process.

entries.label: lamb kidney (raw)
entries.definition: A raw kidney that is obtained from a lamb.

entries.label: haggis
entries.definition: Haggis is a savoury pudding containing sheep's pluck (heart, liver, and lungs); minced with onion, oatmeal, suet, spices, and salt, mixed with stock, and cooked while traditionally encased in the animal's stomach though now often in an artificial casing instead.

entries.label: sheep liver (raw)
entries.definition: A raw liver that is obtained from a sheep.

entries.label: cannelloni
entries.definition: Cannelloni are a cylindrical type of lasagna generally served baked with a filling and covered by a sauce in Italian cuisine.

entries.label: Biltong
entries.definition: Biltong is a form of dried, cured meat that originated in Southern African countrie. Various types of meat are used to produce it, ranging from beef and game meats to fillets of meat cut into strips following the grain of the muscle, or flat pieces sliced across the grain. It is related to beef jerky in that they are both spiced, dried meats; however, the typical ingredients, taste and production

entries.label: duqqa
entries.definition: Duqqa is an Egyptian condiment consisting of a mixture of herbs, nuts (usually hazelnut), and spices. It is typically used as a dip with bread or fresh vegetables for an hors d'œuvre.

entries.label: badufsuki stew
entries.definition: Badufsuki is listed in the USDA SR legacy database as a stew of Hopi cuisine containing pinto beans and hominy grits

aliases.text: farata (in Mauritius, Sri Lanka and the Maldives)
